# Open Bias

> Open Source Reliability Harness for AI Agents.

Open Bias is an AI reliability harness that enforces business rules, compliance policies, and safety constraints on LLM-powered agents at runtime. It is an open source alternative to building custom guardrails or relying on prompt engineering alone for AI safety and policy compliance.

Open Bias works as a transparent proxy between your application and any LLM provider (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, Groq, Together AI, OpenRouter). You define rules in a plain Markdown file called `RULES.md`, and Open Bias evaluates every request and response against those rules — intervening, blocking, or logging violations before they reach users.

System prompts and instruction files become unreliable as you add more rules — models treat instructions as context, not constraints. Open Bias moves enforcement out of the prompt into an independent evaluation layer that does not depend on the model choosing to comply.

- Repository: https://github.com/open-bias/open-bias
- Package: `pip install openbias` — https://pypi.org/project/openbias
- License: Apache 2.0

## What It Enforces

- **Business rules**: Pricing limits, discount caps, data disclosure policies, approval workflows, operational constraints. Agents cannot offer unauthorized discounts, reveal internal pricing, or skip required verification steps.
- **Regulatory compliance**: GDPR data minimization and data subject request routing. EU AI Act transparency, human escalation for high-impact decisions, and traceable explanations.
- **Domain-specific policies**: Customer support (verification before account access, no fabricated refunds or credits, escalation for payments). Healthcare information (no diagnosis claims, emergency escalation, no unsupervised dosing).
- **AI safety and content moderation**: Refuse harmful instructions, protect sensitive data, prevent fabrication. Resist prompt injection, block secret extraction, ignore instruction hijacking from untrusted content.
- **Workflow enforcement**: Multi-step process compliance — verify identity before refund, gather info before escalation. Deterministic state machine enforcement with temporal constraints.
- **Policy evolution**: Capture production traffic, replay against policy candidates, generate and compare variants, human-approve changes before they go live.

## How It Works

Rules are written in plain Markdown and compiled into engine-native artifacts at startup. Open Bias evaluates every LLM request and response against those rules using one or more evaluation engines:

- **Judge engine**: Sidecar LLM evaluates rules independently. Zero critical-path latency in async mode. Best for business rules, safety, compliance.
- **FSM engine**: Finite state machine with temporal constraints. No LLM cost. Best for deterministic workflow enforcement.
- **LLM engine**: LLM-based state classification and drift detection. Best for ambiguous conversational workflows.
- **NeMo engine**: NVIDIA NeMo Guardrails for jailbreak detection, PII filtering, and content moderation.

On violation: intervene (correct next turn, zero latency), block (reject immediately), or shadow (log only). Fail-open by default — the proxy never becomes the bottleneck.

## Rule Presets

Ships with starter rule presets for common enforcement scenarios:

| Category | Preset | Covers |
|----------|--------|--------|
| Compliance | GDPR Privacy | Data minimization, subject request routing, disclosure controls |
| Compliance | EU AI Act | AI transparency, human escalation, anti-manipulation |
| Domain | Customer Support | Account verification, no fabricated credits, payment escalation |
| Domain | Healthcare Information | No diagnosis claims, emergency referral, dosing safety |
| Core | General Safety | Harmful content refusal, data protection, anti-fabrication |
| Core | Prompt Injection | Instruction hijacking resistance, credential protection |

Presets are starter guardrails, not legal advice. Write your own rules in `RULES.md` — any plain Markdown.
